nodes.title: SG-7.8 · Round poller behind a mocked Git interface
nodes.body:
Context: backend/worker/internal has config, store, lock, runner, recovery and report packages but no poller. The backend round.Service.Close already writes snapshot.yaml, records FreezeCommit and moves a Round to CLOSED. Desired behavior: a new poller package pulls the repository through a Git interface, lists the Rounds of the World, reports SCHEDULED and CLOSED Rounds, and closes OPEN Rounds whose end time has passed through a Closer interface that mirrors round.Service.Close. Expected result: unit tests with a fake Git, fake Closer and fake clock prove detection, closing and error handling. Why: Phase 5 needs the worker to see closed Rounds and freeze expired ones.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a Git fake returning SCHEDULED, OPEN and CLOSED Rounds, when Poll runs, then Result.Scheduled and Result.Closed list the matching Round IDs.
- Given an OPEN Round whose EndsAt is not after the clock time, when Poll runs, then Closer.Close is called once for it and its ID is in Result.ClosedNow and Result.Closed.
- Given Git pull fails, when Poll runs, then Poll returns a wrapped error and calls neither ListRounds nor Close.
- Given Close fails for one Round, when Poll runs, then the other Rounds are still processed and the error is returned.


## Scope
- In scope: New package backend/worker/internal/poller with Git, Closer and Clock interfaces and Poller.Poll
- In scope: Unit tests with fakes
- Out of scope: Real Git CLI implementation
- Out of scope: Starting executions from detected Rounds
- Out of scope: Changes to backend/internal/round
- Out of scope: Poll loop wiring in a worker main
- Preserve: backend/internal/round Close and snapshot behavior
- Preserve: Existing worker packages and tests


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22 module github.com/worldseed/storyforge/worker; no new third-party dependencies
- The poller must not import backend/internal packages; the Closer interface mirrors round.Service.Close(ctx, worldID, roundID) error
- No database or queue


## Definition of done
- All acceptance criteria are covered by unit tests that pass with go test ./internal/poller


## Non-functional requirements
- Poll is deterministic and uses only the injected clock


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Poll detects SCHEDULED and CLOSED Rounds through a Git interface
nodes.body:
Context: no poller exists. Desired behavior: Poller.Poll calls Git.Pull then Git.ListRounds(worldID) and returns Result with Scheduled and Closed ID slices in list order. Expected result: the worker can see which Rounds are waiting to open and which are ready for development. Why: later phases start executions from CLOSED Rounds.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Rounds R1 SCHEDULED, R2 OPEN (not expired) and R3 CLOSED, when Poll runs, then Result.Scheduled is [R1] and Result.Closed is [R3].
- Given no Rounds, when Poll runs, then Result slices are empty and the error is nil.
- Given Poll runs, then Git.Pull is called before Git.ListRounds exactly once each.


## Scope
- In scope: Round, Status, Git, Clock, Result, Poller, New, Poll detection
- Out of scope: Closing Rounds
- Preserve: Existing worker packages


## Technical constraints
- Standard library only


## Definition of done
- Detection behavior implemented in backend/worker/internal/poller/poller.go


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Poll closes expired OPEN Rounds through the snapshot-freezing Closer
nodes.body:
Context: round.Service.Close writes the immutable snapshot and moves the Round to CLOSED. Desired behavior: for every OPEN Round with !clock.Now().Before(EndsAt), Poll calls Closer.Close(ctx, worldID, roundID); on success the ID is added to Result.ClosedNow and Result.Closed. Expected result: expired Rounds are frozen without the poller touching contribution files. Why: contributions must freeze at the Round end.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an OPEN Round with EndsAt equal to or before the clock time, when Poll runs, then Close is called once with that world and round ID.
- Given an OPEN Round with EndsAt after the clock time, when Poll runs, then Close is not called.
- Given a successful close, then the ID appears in Result.ClosedNow and Result.Closed.


## Scope
- In scope: Closer interface and expiry check in Poll
- Out of scope: Snapshot writing, which stays in backend/internal/round
- Preserve: round.Service.Close


## Technical constraints
- Time comes only from the injected Clock


## Definition of done
- Expiry closing implemented in poller.go


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Poll aborts on Git failures and keeps going after a Close failure
nodes.body:
Context: the worker polls repeatedly and must survive partial failures. Desired behavior: a Pull error returns Result{} and an error wrapping the cause with prefix 'poller: pull'; a ListRounds error returns 'poller: list rounds'; a Close failure is collected with errors.Join as 'poller: close <id>' while remaining Rounds are processed and the failed ID is excluded from Closed. A nil Closer with an expired Round yields an error instead of a panic.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Pull returns an error, when Poll runs, then the error satisfies errors.Is against it and ListRounds and Close are not called.
- Given ListRounds returns an error, then Poll returns it wrapped and Close is not called.
- Given two expired Rounds where the first Close fails, then the second is still closed, the returned error wraps the first failure and Result.Closed lacks the first ID.
- Given a nil Closer and an expired Round, then Poll returns an error and does not panic.


## Scope
- In scope: Error handling in Poll
- Out of scope: Retry or backoff
- Preserve: Detection and closing behavior


## Technical constraints
- Use fmt.Errorf with %w and errors.Join


## Definition of done
- Error semantics implemented in poller.go


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create the file with package doc, Status string constants StatusScheduled, StatusOpen, StatusClosed, struct Round{ID, WorldID string; Status Status; EndsAt time.Time}, interface Git{Pull(ctx) error; ListRounds(ctx, worldID string) ([]Round, error)}, interface Closer{Close(ctx, worldID, roundID string) error}, interface Clock{Now() time.Time}, and struct Result{Scheduled, Closed, ClosedNow []string}.

steps.expected: Poll returns the detected IDs and a nil error for healthy fakes.

nodes.summary: Add the expiry case to Poll that calls Closer.Close and records ClosedNow
nodes.description: Extend Poller.Poll in poller.go with an OPEN case using the injected Clock.
acceptance_criteria: Expired OPEN Rounds are closed once; non-expired are not.
Closed IDs appear in ClosedNow and Closed.

out_of_scope: Error handling beyond collecting Close errors

technical_constraints: Use p.clock.Now().Before(r.EndsAt) for the expiry check
definition_of_done: poller.go builds and expired Rounds are closed

steps.lines: after the StatusClosed case of the switch written by act-detect
steps.action: Add case r.Status == StatusOpen && !p.clock.Now().Before(r.EndsAt): call p.closer.Close(ctx, p.worldID, r.ID); on nil error append r.ID to res.ClosedNow and res.Closed; on error append fmt.Errorf("poller: close %s: %w", r.ID, err) to a local errs slice. Return res and errors.Join(errs...) at the end. Convert the switch to a tagless switch to allow the condition.
steps.code:
case r.Status == StatusOpen && !p.clock.Now().Before(r.EndsAt):
	if err := p.closer.Close(ctx, p.worldID, r.ID); err != nil {
		errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("poller: close %s: %w", r.ID, err))
		continue
	}
	res.ClosedNow = append(res.ClosedNow, r.ID)
	res.Closed = append(res.Closed, r.ID)
steps.expected: Expired OPEN Rounds are closed once and reported.
